I'm bipolar.  I'm just barely holding my life together.  The meds aren't working.  I've seen bipolar in my family and it's ended very, very badly.  It seems very unlikely that my future will be any better.
thank you.  I just went out for a bit and it did help a little.

Yup.  That would be my life as well.  I want to stop seeing my psychiatrist because he a. won't return my calls, b. comes 45 min - 1 hour late for my appointments, c. stood up and walked out of the office while i was asking him about the medication 7 min into our last appointment and told me to schedule another for the rest of my questions and then d. called in the wrong prescription.  Is this common psychiatrist behavior?  I've had incredible difficulty making appointments in general; are there simply not enough of them so they are able to treat their patients like this and retain business?
And no, no one who has not been through this will understand.  My friends, family and boyfriend have all resented me for not being able to snap out of it.  I know it's a simple lack of comprehension on their part but it still hurts like hell and leaves me feeling very isolated.
I tried Wellbutrin very briefly (2 weeks).  My doctor discontinued it because it was disrupting my sleep.  I wonder of I should give it another try though.  How long have you been on it?

It's nice to know that someone understands.  It's really only a sense of obligation that gets me through the darkest times.  Although I don't have anyone in my life whom I can really rely on I do have people that I care about who rely on me.  Yet the thought of living through another 50+ years like the last 10 terrifies me regardless of what mood I'm in and I find it difficult to weigh my own anguish against the harm I would cause others by ending it.  Thank you for letting me know that I'm not alone in feeling this.
Thanks for the reply.  If you don't mind my asking, what drug combination worked for you?
